Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: There is no explicit marker for the absolutive case.
curated_comment: U'wa (ango1257, ISO uwa, Chibchan, Colombia/Venezuela) shows consistent ergative-absolutive alignment documented in Casilimas Rojas (1995). The language uses a postpositional ergative marker {-at} on transitive agents. All 24 features verified against the PDF. Key updates from original annotation: GB409_19 changed from '?' to 1 (inanimate A like comején/termite takes {-at} ergative, p.186 ex.6.7b). GB409_11=0 retained: original citation (p.126) incorrectly references interrogative pronouns; no positive evidence for ERG in non-indicative moods was found, so the absence is maintained as 0. GB409_22=0 confirmed: no additional conditioning factors documented. Glottocode ango1257 is correct; the previously proposed uuwa1243 (Uw Oykangand, Pama-Nyungan, Australia) is an unrelated language.

Comment: Ergative alignment applies to topical A arguments.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in main clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Ergative alignment occurs in non-main clauses such as relative clauses.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
